# drawgen: the full text of drawgen.co

Every page, in order. Product examples on the site are illustrative, with made-up generic data.

URL: https://drawgen.co/
Title: drawgen: quotes built on data, not memory
Description: drawgen connects the systems your data already lives in, so every quote is faster to send and priced on what similar jobs actually cost.

For manufacturers who build to order

# Quotes built on data, not memory.
drawgen connects the systems your data already lives in, so every quote is faster to send and priced on what similar jobs actually cost.
Talk to us The drawgen vision, 0:23
Illustrative example: a starting price of €19,800 built from the 3D model, purchase history and three similar past jobs, waiting for your estimator's approval. Made-up data, not real output.
Vision

## Manufacturing has evolved. The systems behind it haven't.
Your data already exists. It sits in the CAD model, the ERP, past quotes and one or two people's heads. drawgen connects it, so every quote is faster to send and priced on what similar jobs actually cost.
The drawgen vision, 0:23 On screen in the video
- Manufacturing has evolved.
- The systems behind it should too.
- Less friction.
- More flow.
- drawgen.
- Manufacturing // reimagined
Play with sound
The drawgen record

## One record per part, across every system you run.
What you paid is in your ERP. What you quoted is in your CRM. What the part actually is sits in the CAD model. The drawgen record joins them, so a price you paid last year attaches to the same part in the job you are quoting now. Nobody types anything in. The drawgen record
Illustrative example: one part as the CAD model, the ERP and the CRM each name it, joined into one drawgen record. Made-up data.
McKinsey names a lack of spending transparency as the first of five things holding back procurement at mid-size firms.
Source:
- McKinsey, How medium-size enterprises can better manage sourcing, 2023 (opens in a new tab)

## What it costs you, and why now
Time
2 weeks
of real work, in a three-and-a-half-month order at a German machine builder. The rest was questions, clarification and waiting.
Source:
- Staufen AG, lean order fulfilment in machinery and plant engineering, 2018 (opens in a new tab)
In 2023, Fraunhofer studied the quote process at a German special machine builder. Prices in Excel, quotes rebuilt from old ones in Word, and colleagues asked for every cost and delivery date.
Source: Fraunhofer IEM, Systems Engineering for the offer phase in special purpose machinery, DfX-Symposium 2023 (opens in a new tab)
Margin
−40% to +70%
In a study of tool and die making, quoted cost against actual cost ran from minus 40% to plus 70%. Different trade, same one-off, engineering-led work.
Source:
- WZL RWTH Aachen and Werkzeugbau-Akademie, Erfolgreich kalkulieren im Werkzeugbau, 2015 (opens in a new tab)
Knowledge
The same in every market
The person who knows what a job really costs is retiring faster than they are replaced.
Source:
- UK: 55,000 manufacturing vacancies unfilled. Make UK, 2025 (opens in a new tab)
- US: up to 1.9 million manufacturing jobs unfilled by 2033. Deloitte and The Manufacturing Institute, 2024 (opens in a new tab)
- Australia: about 70,000 engineers retiring this decade. Engineers Australia, 2026 (opens in a new tab)
- Germany: 178,000 short by 2034. IW Köln for the Impuls-Stiftung, 2024 (opens in a new tab)
Speed
Years to months
Chinese manufacturers have compressed development cycles from years to months while staying 20 to 30% cheaper.
Source:
- Roland Berger, China's cost and speed advantage, 2026 (opens in a new tab)
- Your CAD files never leave your machine
- Nothing estimated, anything unclear flagged
- Everything editable, nothing sent unchecked
- Built for manufacturers who build to order

## Built for your industry
What McKinsey calls low-volume, high-complexity manufacturing: machines built in ones and tens, not thousands.
Source:
- McKinsey, low-volume high-complexity manufacturing series (opens in a new tab)
- A one-off automated assembly machine in an aluminium profile frame, half built on the floor of a machine builder, with machined parts laid out on the bench beside it. Special-purpose machinery Every machine is a one-off. The quote should not be a guess.
- A long roller conveyor with steel box-section side frames and a gear motor, with cut profiles and bearing units stacked behind it. Material handling and conveyors Frames and profiles, measured off the model, not re-measured.
- A stainless case-packing machine under final assembly, guard doors open, pneumatic cylinders and an infeed conveyor with cardboard cases. Packaging machinery Packaging lines priced on your history, not your memory.
- A robotic cell being commissioned: a six-axis robot with a parallel gripper over a welded fixture table, inside mesh safety fencing. Automation and robotic cells A BOM that is right the first time, bought-out and custom.
- Primed wide-flange steel beams and a large welded platform frame with thick base plates, resting on timber blocks in a fabrication shop. Heavy fabrication and steel Big steel, measured off the model, not with a tape.
- A steel lifting beam hanging from a chain hoist on a pillar jib crane, with test weights on the floor below. Lifting equipment Quoted with the engineering in it, not discovered after.

## Built to give your team time back, not to replace anyone.
It takes the repetitive work off your engineers and estimators: the measuring, the retyping, the chasing. The judgement stays with them: tolerances, datums, what to quote and who to buy from. Everything it produces is editable, and nothing goes out until your people have checked it.

URL: https://drawgen.co/product/record/
Title: The drawgen record: one record per part
Description: One record per part, joined on the part's shape rather than its number, so it works even when part numbers are a mess. Your CAD files stay on your machine.

drawgen Product The drawgen record
The drawgen record

# One record per part, across every system you run.
What you paid is in your ERP. What you quoted is in your CRM. What the part actually is sits in the CAD model. The drawgen record joins them, so a price you paid last year attaches to the same part in the job you are quoting now. Nobody types anything in. Talk to us
Illustrative example: one part as the CAD model, the ERP and the CRM each name it, joined into one drawgen record. Made-up data.

## What it is
One record per part, joined on the part's shape rather than its number, so it works even when part numbers are a mess.

## Two ways in

### The add-in
inside SOLIDWORKS, used by the engineer. Produces the BOM and the drawings, and quietly writes the part record.

### The platform
in the browser, used by the MD, sales and purchasing. Holds every job side by side, joined to purchase history.

## What crosses
The measurements, not the models. Your CAD files stay on your machine, and the whole thing can run on your own server.
McKinsey names a lack of spending transparency as the first of five things holding back procurement at mid-size firms.
Source:
- McKinsey, How medium-size enterprises can better manage sourcing, 2023 (opens in a new tab)

drawgen Product BOM

# Every part in the assembly, measured, in one BOM.
BOM From the model
Material, size, mass, surface area and quantity for every part, plus what to make and what to buy. Your engineer reviews it before it goes anywhere.
Connects to Connects to the 3D model, through the add-in. Talk to us
Illustrative example
Illustrative example: a BOM for a generic assembly, every part measured off the model with material, size, mass and quantity, tagged make or buy, with one part flagged for the engineer. Made-up data.

## You get
- Every part with material, profile, length, mass, surface area and quantity
- Every part tagged as bought-out or made to your drawing, and what kind of supplier makes it
- Which parts repeat inside the job and across jobs
- An export in your format
Built on the drawgen record

### Problem
Problem
Designers spend 19% of their time, about a day a week, finding, recreating and translating data.
Source:
- Tech-Clarity, Saving time in CAD design (opens in a new tab)
Problem
One engineer extracted 33 parts from a model by hand. Two to three hours for one assembly.
Source:
- From our conversations with manufacturers

## How it works
- Open the assembly.
- One click.
- Every part measured off the solid and classified.
- The BOM comes back ready to check.

drawgen Product Drawings

# Manufacturing drawings, derived from the solid.
Drawings From the model
One dimensioned sheet per part, editable, in your own drawing format. Anything it cannot determine is flagged, and your engineer finishes it.
Connects to Connects to the 3D model. Talk to us
Illustrative example
Illustrative example: a dimensioned drawing sheet of a generic plate, 600 by 400, with four holes and a pocket whose depth is flagged for the engineer, and a change record for revision B. Made-up data.

## You get
- One sheet per part, editable, in your format
- Anything unclear flagged, never filled in
- A change record showing which sheets a new revision affects
Built on the drawgen record

### Problem
Problem
Five to 45 minutes a part, and one drawing in four comes back.
Source:
- From our conversations with manufacturers
Problem
Quality-related costs are often put at 15 to 20% of sales, a long-standing rule of thumb in quality management.
Source:
- ASQ, cost of quality (opens in a new tab)

drawgen Product Costing

# Data-driven quotes that match what the job actually costs.
Costing From connected systems
Every price built on something that actually happened: a price you paid, a job you finished, a part you already built.
Connects to Connects to your ERP and purchase history, your past quotes, your cost sheets, and the model. Talk to us
Illustrative example
Illustrative example: a starting price of €19,800 split into parts measured off the model, bought-out parts at last prices paid, and assembly from three similar past jobs, with each past job's quoted and actual cost. Made-up data.

## You get
- Similar past jobs, what you quoted and what they actually cost
- Where the margin went on the ones that went wrong
- A defensible starting price for the next one
- Duplicate parts, to merge
- Over-specified parts, to re-spec
- Overpriced parts, to take to RFQ
Built on the drawgen record

### Problem
Problem
In a study of tool and die making, quoted cost against actual cost ran from minus 40% to plus 70%.
Source:
- WZL RWTH Aachen and Werkzeugbau-Akademie, Erfolgreich kalkulieren im Werkzeugbau, 2015 (opens in a new tab)
Problem
SMEs often fail to identify basic price variances.
Source:
- McKinsey, How medium-size enterprises can better manage sourcing, 2023 (opens in a new tab)
Why it matters
A carefully worked-out quote costs real money, and the effort spent on quotes that do not win has to be carried by the orders that do.
Source:
- Fraunhofer IEM, DfX-Symposium 2023 (opens in a new tab)
Why it matters
In Fraunhofer's assessment, the improvements a 2007 survey of 281 machine and plant builders asked for, better calculation bases, transparency and a continuous flow of information, have still not been properly put in place.
Source:
- Fraunhofer IEM, 2023, on the VDI survey of 2007 (opens in a new tab)

## How it works
- Connect your ERP and past quotes.
- Every past job is joined to its parts.
- A new job is compared against the ones like it.
- Your estimator gets a starting price with the reasons behind it.
Costing

drawgen Product Sourcing

# Buy on what you have actually paid, not on habit.
Sourcing From connected systems
See which supplier has been cheapest and fastest for each kind of part, and send every RFQ as one complete package.
Connects to Connects to your ERP purchase history and supplier records, and the quotes that come back by email. Talk to us
Illustrative example
Illustrative example: suppliers compared on your own purchase history for three kinds of part, and RFQ packages waiting for your buyer to check and send. Made-up data.

## You get
- Which supplier has been cheapest and fastest for this kind of part
- One RFQ package per supplier, right drawings attached, quantities correct
- Returned quotes lined up against the BOM
- Where you buy the same thing from four places, and where you depend on one
Built on the drawgen record

### Problem
Problem
External spend is typically 50 to 80% of a company's cost base.
Source:
- McKinsey, A new era for procurement (opens in a new tab)
Problem
If material is around half your costs and your margin is around 6%, taking 1% off what you pay for material is close to an 8% rise in profit. The thinner your margin, the more that 1% is worth.
Source:
- Arithmetic.
Why it matters
McKinsey's experience is that digital procurement can deliver as much as an additional 3 to 10 percent in annual cost savings.
Source:
- McKinsey, Shifting the dial in procurement, 2019 (opens in a new tab)
Why it matters
At mid-size firms, category managers spend their days on transactional work, while large-company peers spend theirs on negotiation.
Source:
- McKinsey, How medium-size enterprises can better manage sourcing, 2023 (opens in a new tab)

## How it works
- The BOM tags every part by who makes it.
- Parts are grouped into one package per supplier.
- Your team checks and sends.
- Quotes come back and line up against the BOM.
Sourcing
- drawgenhelp@gmail.com
- LinkedIn (opens in a new tab) Talk to us

- Automation and robotic cells Bought-out parts grouped into one RFQ package per supplier, with quantities from the BOM.
- Heavy fabrication and steel Steel and plate bought from the supplier your record shows has been cheapest and fastest.
- Lifting equipment Plate and beams bought on what each supplier has actually charged, not on who you used last.

Title: Material handling and conveyors | drawgen
Description: Frames, supports and guarding redrawn and re-measured on every job, even when half of it matches the last one.

drawgen Industries Material handling and conveyors
For material handling and conveyors

# Frames and profiles, measured off the model, not re-measured.
Frames, supports and guarding redrawn and re-measured on every job, even when half of it matches the last one. Talk to us
Today With drawgen
1 Profiles re-measured by hand
2 Measured off the model
Bought and made
Profiles, plate, bearings.
Worked example
A conveyor side frame in box section.
Checked
Your engineer
What you get

## Frames and profiles measured once, off the model.
drawgen reads every profile, plate and bearing straight from the assembly. The parts that match the last job show up as repeats, so nobody measures them twice.
- BOM Every profile with its length and mass, with plate and bearings in the same BOM.
- Drawings Editable sheets for side frames, supports and guarding, in your own format.
- Costing A price for the next conveyor built on what similar conveyors actually cost you.
- Sourcing Profiles and bearings bought from the supplier that has actually been cheapest and fastest.

Title: Packaging machinery | drawgen
